results.term_definition: A star with spectral type "B". Astronomers identify B-type stars by the presence of neutral helium lines along with hydrogen lines in their spectra. They have typical (effective) temperatures between around 10,000 kelvins (K) to 30,000 K. Compared to other stars, they appear bluish white to human eyes unless interstellar or atmospheric reddening is important. Examples of B-type stars include Regulus in Leo, Rigel in Orion, and Spica in Virgo.
